sections.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
sections.abstract: Frames semi-supervised learning as a program-search task for machine-learning-engineering agents, finding gains over human-designed baselines in 8 of 12 settings while identifying program selection as a major bottleneck.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce AgentSSL and ProgramSelectBench, reporting up to +21.8% over the strongest human-engineered baselines in 8/12 settings and up to a 47% performance drop when selecting with the agent's feedback metric.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper's discussion says SSL is not always preferable and that on the ecology tasks the supervised AgentSL baseline matches AgentSSL; the authors describe the framework as an initial baseline, not a performance ceiling.

sections.title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
sections.abstract: Defines one-sided verifiability, where a checker can reliably reject some failures but cannot certify accepted outputs, and proposes NOPO, which updates from trusted negatives without directly rewarding non-falsified candidates.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine reference-relative suppression of verified negatives with a group-level non-falsified-support weight and report improved pass@k over baselines under unit-test, constraint-check, and LLM self-verifiers.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that negative-only learning specifies what to avoid but not where probability mass should move; results also weaken when a verifier has low negative recall, as in their OlympiadBench setup.

sections.title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate
sections.abstract: Introduces DiVR, a verifier that uses a diffusion language model's hidden states and trajectory outcomes to decide when to regenerate a block and which alternative to keep, improving reported accuracy on five reasoning benchmarks at additional decoding cost.
sections.claimed_contribution: For an SFT LLaDA-8B-Base model, the authors report average accuracy rising from 35.3% to 43.4% at 1.9–3.5× greedy-decoding cost, versus 3.8–7.4× for the cited search baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The accuracy increase uses more inference compute than greedy decoding, and the headline result is tied to the tested generators and five reasoning benchmarks.

sections.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
sections.abstract: Studies goal representations in LLMs in a multi-subtask coding setting, localizing a next-subgoal encoding to sparse attention heads and testing its causal role and transfer between environments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors identify attention-head outputs that encode upcoming subgoals, report causal effects on next actions, and propose a non-recurrent account in which the model rereads task goals and compares them with progress in context.
sections.unique_caveat: The experiments use a constructed coding setting; the abstract does not establish that the same goal encoding mechanism generalizes across broader tasks or model families.

sections.title: LiveGeo: Benchmarking Geographic Agents in Continuously Evolving Worlds
sections.abstract: Presents GeoWorld and LiveGeo, a platform and benchmark for testing whether LLM agents acquire current geographic evidence, check whether it remains valid as the world changes, and revise decisions accordingly.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a controllable geographic environment with evolving external states and verifiable histories, and report that current agents struggle to maintain correct decisions as those states change.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is conducted through GeoWorld/LiveGeo; the abstract does not report deployment results in live geographic operations.

sections.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
sections.abstract: Uses matched-compute pretraining comparisons to separate the effects of visual pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and where that capacity enters a multimodal model, finding that jointly trained capacity matters more than a pretrained visual prior in the tested settings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that dedicated vision capacity is useful, need not be pretrained separately, and can be placed in early in-fusion modules that perform comparably to a pre-fusion encoder while reducing time to first token.
sections.unique_caveat: The claims are bounded by the paper's pretraining framework and visual-question-answering/language benchmark suite; they do not establish that the same design wins for every multimodal task or compute regime.

sections.title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
sections.abstract: Proposes a coding-agent framework that values repository memory by its effect on subsequent tasks and trains the actor to use memory when it saves effort, reporting improved resolution with fewer steps and cache-aware tokens on ChainSWE.
sections.claimed_contribution: On ChainSWE, the authors report a 21.0% to 25.7% resolve-rate increase for a 27B actor, with 17% fewer steps and 11% fewer total cache-aware tokens.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported result is on ChainSWE with a 27B actor; the abstract does not establish that the same gains hold across other repositories, task distributions, or model scales.

sections.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
sections.abstract: Presents CRAM, a learned Hopfield-and-Tank-style energy model that solves the paper's Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique tests with low reported training time and inference FLOPs, and contrasts it with looped reasoning models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 99.996% Sudoku-Extreme and 100% Maze-Unique test accuracy, and at least 282× fewer inference FLOPs than looped baselines at matched Sudoku accuracy.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly caution that Sudoku and Maze may be trivially solvable benchmarks for evaluating the scalability of looped reasoning methods; the results do not establish comparable gains on harder reasoning tasks.
